agree.reason: The nurse's firsthand line-outside-the-door framing, the AAP recommendation and the neighboring district's results are persuasive, and each named concern gets a concrete answer, though a skeptical board member may still want a funding source and evidence that early supervision is feasible.

honest.reason: It wisely refuses to promise a graduation-rate gain, but it adds facts not in the brief (teens need eight to ten hours, the 11 p.m. body-clock shift, attendance as an early warning sign), and 'something about 7:25 is making our kids sick' implies more causation than the visit log shows.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly turns 640/890 into about 72 percent and the 84 percent graduation rate into roughly one in six students not finishing on time, but it leaves the 412-vs-369 first-period gap unquantified and gives the $180,000 no per-day or per-student scale.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is described in terms of its ongoing costs (tardies, nurse visits, lost class time), but those costs are asserted rather than quantified, and the brief gives no trend data, so the comparison stays general.

qualification.reason: The only hedge, 'I can't promise a later bell will raise our graduation rate by a set amount,' is honest but names no measure, date or threshold the reader could check later, such as first-period tardies or attendance after one year.

objections.reason: Athletics, 8 a.m. drop-offs and the $180,000 bus cost are each acknowledged and answered with a proposal, though the early-supervision fix has its own unaddressed cost and the budget answer stops at asking the board to name a source.

fit.reason: It is a properly structured op-ed with a headline, a first-person voice, a call to vote by April 14 and a byline, and it runs close to the 650-word limit.
